newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Telekom says ready to invest in Telkom.
newsitem.headline: Telekom says ready to invest in Telkom.

text.p: Telekom Malaysia Bhd, committed to spending around $500 million for a stake in South Africa's Telkom, is ready to invest more if required, Malaysian national news agency Bernama reported on Friday.

"Telekom Malaysia's liquidity is very good, and strictly speaking, we can come out with the funds as our reserves are sufficent to cover the investment," Bernama quoted Telekom chief executive Mohamed Said Mohamed Ali as saying.
Telekom is teaming up with U.S.-based SBC Communications Inc to take a joint 30 percent stake in Telkom for a total of $1.26 billion. Telekom's own portion was 12 percent valued at $504 million.
Telekom was considering various steps to raise the required funds, Mohamed Said told reporters after the company's extraordinary general meeting.
He added that the company had access to facilities at "a very good rate" if it had to seek offshore funds.
Mohamed Said said he expected Telkom to go for a public listing in three years.
